by_question.answer: The oracle is real. It measures the rendered mix: TimelineMixStream (audio.rs) through render_at_speed (score varispeed.rs), neither of which references annotate, retime's law or source_to_timeline (git grep finds none). heard_at is the energy centroid of the rendered samples; the Hann pulse is symmetric, so reversal does not shift it. By hand the read stands 1/|speed| mix samples after the mix: at(i) = end - 1 - i gives source tick s at start + (so - s - 1 sample)/r against the read's start + (so - s)/r. That is 0.0005F at -1, 0.0010F at -1/2, 0.0003F at -2, below WITHIN 0.002F (3.84 samples). It cannot pass with the bug: on all six QUARTERS at all four reversed speeds, law and continuous differ by at least 0.25F (smallest: -2, q46: 6.00 against 6.25 frames in). Red log confirms the table: red-proof-r58 line 4806 region, worst 0.999, 0.500, 1.999, 0.666.

second_read.ruling_assessment: The pair ruling is right for a unit of exactly two clips: by reading, and by the builder's runs against the mix and frame_layers, the pair stays in sync at -1, -2 and -1/2 and nothing underflows. It is incomplete as a rule for a unit. Every member is aligned against the anchor alone, so two members meet only through the anchor, and their relative position is the difference of two reads that can be under two laws. No per-pair rule can close that: against a forward anchor the frame law is needed for a reversed picture (16F, frame_layers) and the continuous mapping for reversed sound (15F, the mix), and those two rows are a frame apart by construction. Not wrong; it needs a sentence saying where it stops.

by_question.answer: The pinned case is correct sound-to-sound alignment, not a defect in itself. Reversed sound's clap is heard 27.9995F, forward sound 28.0000F, one sample apart (green-pr59 log line 5099). It is outside frame 2's presentation only by the half-open edge: the tick the anchor's read names is the frame's exclusive end. Yes, one operation can give inconsistent results across its members: from a reversed picture anchor the same clap is heard 27.9995F on reversed sound and 27.0000F on forward sound, 40 ms apart inside one operation, both under frame 2 (line 5097; by hand 80 ms at -1/2 and 20 ms at -2). The result depends on which clip is the anchor: the same three clips put forward sound at 25F or 26F relative to the unmoved pair (tests :606, :613). That is new: at 4ffe1b06, 89bbf702 and for all forward clips, relative positions do not depend on the anchor. It does not depend on member order: each offset is a pure function of anchor and member (:601-603), clip_ids order only orders the output, and settle touches one member per track. Also path-dependent: sync(V, A) then sync(A, B) gives B 26F, sync(V, B) gives 25F. Named in the lane notes, and 'the anchor's position can differ by member' is in the docs and DESCRIPTOR; the 40 ms between two sounds and the anchor-dependence are not spelled out for a model. F-SR-2.

by_question.answer: Independent, yes. Sound is the centroid of the rendered mix through heard_on (:465-469) and picture is frame_layers at the start of the timeline frame (:449-455); neither calls the marker read, and placed positions are hand numbers. Mutations read from their logs: anchor None fails 6 of 28, dropped condition fails 1 of 28, at :676, refused not_frame_aligned. One test is enough for the mutation and thin for the condition.
